title: Triple Point provides £17m facility for Fulham development
summary:
Triple Point has originated a £17m development finance facility for a mixed-use residential scheme in Fulham, marking the largest single loan the lender's property development team has originated. The facility will fund construction of 31 apartments across two blocks alongside two commercial units off the King's Road.

title: Investor secures £335k bridge to settle enforcement order
summary:
A London-based property investor has secured a £335,000 bridging loan against an unencumbered buy-to-let property in Dollis Hill to meet a court-ordered liability arising from a planning enforcement dispute. The 24-month facility was provided by TAB against a property valued at £1 million, representing a loan-to-value ratio of 33.5%.

title: Sales progression franchise model launches across UK
summary:
A sales progression company has launched what it describes as the UK's first franchise model dedicated to the sector, targeting estate agencies and experienced progressors across England and Wales. Property Progressors will establish a network of locally based sales progressors operating under franchise agreements within designated territories.

title: Conveyancing identified as top transaction bottleneck
summary:
Conveyancing has been identified as the primary factor slowing property transactions, with 42% of recent homebuyers citing it as the biggest barrier to smooth completions. Research from Lyons Bowe Solicitors found slow communication between conveyancers was the leading cause of delays, significantly outweighing concerns about property chains.

title: Letting agents identify tasks requiring human expertise over AI
summary:
A survey of lettings professionals has identified five core areas where human expertise remains essential, despite the growing adoption of artificial intelligence in the property sector. Research conducted by Propoly found that relationship building, handling disputes, and assessing complex situations are tasks least suited to AI automation.

title: Landlord sentiment on Renters’ Rights Act shows modest shift
summary:
Landlord concerns about the Renters' Rights Act have decreased from 76% to 69% in the four months since implementation. Mortgage Advice Bureau reported over £1 billion in buy-to-let lending between May and August 2026, though more than 60% of landlords report ongoing challenges with the new requirements.

title: Rental competition reaches 30 enquiries per property in hotspots
summary:
Rental competition in Britain's most sought-after areas has reached 30 enquiries per property, according to new data from Rightmove. Birkenhead and Wallasey on the Wirral recorded the highest levels of tenant competition, with typical monthly rents of £874 and £975 respectively.

title: Southampton agency expands homelessness scheme across south coast
summary:
A Southampton-based lettings agency is expanding its homelessness prevention programme to Bournemouth and Portsmouth after securing 532 tenancies for homeless households in the past year. SDM Property operates a model that connects private landlords with councils to provide settled accommodation for people living in temporary or emergency housing.

title: Tax experts question stamp duty on £265m property sale
summary:
Tax specialists have raised questions about the stamp duty paid on the £265 million sale of Providence House in Chelsea, Britain's most expensive residential property transaction. Analysis suggests the transaction structure may have reduced the stamp duty liability by approximately £18.5 million.
